rotational-kinematics-s2.title: A ceiling fan switched on, then off
rotational-kinematics-s2.text: A sensor records the angular velocity of a ceiling fan, counterclockwise positive, as it is switched on, runs, and is switched off.

items.q: What is the wheel’s angular velocity at the end of the 3.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that is ½αt, a mix of two equations. Starting from rest, ω = ω₀ + αt = 0 + αt.

why.correct: From rest, ω = ω₀ + αt = 0 + (2.0 rad/s²)(3.0 s) = 6.0 rad/s.

items.q: Through what angle, in radians, does the chalk mark turn during the 3.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the final angular velocity in rad/s, not the angle turned. Use θ = ω₀t + ½αt².
Value: that is the angle in revolutions. The question asks for radians: θ = ½αt².

why.correct: θ = ω₀t + ½αt² = 0 + ½(2.0 rad/s²)(3.0 s)² = 9.0 rad.

items.q: About how many revolutions does the wheel make in the 3.0 s?
options: 1.4 rev
9.0 rev
2.9 rev
0.70 rev

why.correct: One revolution is 2π rad, so 9.0 rad ÷ 2π = 1.43, about 1.4 rev.
options: Right: 9.0 rad ÷ 2π rad per revolution = 1.4 rev.
This treats each radian as a whole turn. One revolution is 2π rad, about 6.28 rad.
This divides by π instead of 2π. A full turn is 2π rad.
This halves the correct value. A revolution is 2π rad, not 4π rad.

items.q: A second chalk mark is drawn halfway between the first mark and the axle. During the same 3.0 s, its angular displacement is
options: the same as the first mark’s
half the first mark’s
twice the first mark’s
one quarter of the first mark’s

why.correct: The wheel is a rigid system: every point on it turns through the same angle in the same time, so both marks have the same angular displacement (9.0 rad), the same ω and the same α.
options: Right: a rigid wheel turns as one piece, so every mark turns through the same angle.
Halving the distance from the axle changes how far the mark travels, not the angle it turns through.
Being closer to the axle does not make a mark turn through more angle; the wheel turns as one piece.
No square law applies here: every mark on a rigid wheel turns through the same angle.

items.q: The wheel keeps the same angular acceleration but runs for 6.0 s instead of 3.0 s, starting from rest. Its angular displacement is
options: 4 times as large
2 times as large
the same
8 times as large

why.correct: From rest, θ = ½αt². With α fixed, θ ∝ t², so twice the time gives 2² = 4 times the angle (36 rad).
options: Right: from rest θ = ½αt², so doubling t multiplies θ by 2² = 4.
That would be true at constant ω. With constant α from rest, θ grows with t².
A longer time at the same α gives more turning, not the same.
θ depends on t², not t³.

items.q: What is the fan’s angular acceleration from 0 to 4.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides time by angular velocity. α = Δω/Δt, the slope of the ω-t graph.

why.correct: α = Δω/Δt = (12.0 rad/s − 0)/(4.0 s) = 3.0 rad/s², the slope of the graph.

items.q: Through what angle does the fan turn from 0 to 16.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: that uses 12.0 rad/s for the whole 16.0 s. The fan is slower while it speeds up and slows down; take the area under the graph.
Value: that is the constant-speed part only. Add the two triangles where the fan speeds up and slows down.

why.correct: The angle is the area under the ω-t graph: ½(4.0 s)(12.0 rad/s) + (6.0 s)(12.0 rad/s) + ½(6.0 s)(12.0 rad/s) = 24 + 72 + 36 = 132 rad.

items.q: Which describes the fan from 10.0 s to 16.0 s, with counterclockwise positive?
options: Turning counterclockwise and slowing down
Turning clockwise and speeding up
Turning counterclockwise and speeding up
At rest, since α is negative

why.correct: ω is positive (counterclockwise) but decreasing toward zero, so the angular acceleration is negative, opposite to ω: the fan slows down until it stops at 16.0 s.
options: Right: ω stays positive while its size falls, so α is negative.
ω is still positive in this interval, so the fan has not reversed.
ω is getting smaller, so the fan is slowing down.
A negative α means ω is decreasing, not that the fan has stopped; it stops at 16.0 s.

items.q: What is the fan’s angular acceleration at t = 12.0 s?
options: −2.0 rad/s²
+2.0 rad/s²
8.0 rad/s²
0 rad/s²

why.correct: α is the slope of the ω-t graph. From 10.0 s to 16.0 s it is (0 − 12.0 rad/s)/(6.0 s) = -2.0 rad/s², the same at every instant in that interval.
options: Right: the slope from 10.0 s to 16.0 s is −12.0 rad/s ÷ 6.0 s.
The size is right, but ω is falling, so the slope is negative.
That is the value of ω at 12.0 s, read off the graph, not its slope.
The graph is sloping at 12.0 s, so ω is changing and α is not zero.

items.q: How many radians are in one full revolution?
options: 2π rad
π rad
360 rad
1 rad

why.correct: An angle in radians is (distance along the circle) ÷ (radius). A full turn covers the whole circumference, 2πr, so it is 2πr/r = 2π rad.
options: Right: the full circumference is 2π times the radius.
π rad is half a turn, 180°.
360 is the number of degrees in a turn, not radians.
One radian is about 57°, much less than a full turn.

items.q: A record turntable spins at 45 revolutions per minute. What is its angular velocity in rad/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that is revolutions per second. Multiply by 2π rad per revolution.
Value: that is degrees per second. Use 2π rad per revolution, not 360°.

why.correct: ω = (45 rev/min)(2π rad/rev)(1 min/60 s) = 4.71 rad/s, about 4.7 rad/s.

items.q: Counterclockwise is positive. A wheel has a negative angular velocity and a positive angular acceleration. What is it doing?
options: Turning clockwise and slowing down
Turning clockwise and speeding up
Turning counterclockwise and slowing down
Turning counterclockwise and speeding up

why.correct: The sign of ω gives the direction of turning (negative: clockwise). When α has the opposite sign, ω moves toward zero, so the wheel slows, just as a car with v and a of opposite signs slows.
options: Right: ω and α have opposite signs, so the size of ω is shrinking.
Speeding up needs α with the same sign as ω.
A negative ω means clockwise turning.
The sign of ω, not α, gives the direction of turning.

items.q: A wheel turning counterclockwise at 8.0 rad/s slows at a steady rate and stops in 5.0 s. Counterclockwise is positive. What is its angular acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides time by angular velocity. α = Δω/Δt.

why.correct: α = Δω/Δt = (0 − 8.0 rad/s)/(5.0 s) = -1.6 rad/s². It is negative because the wheel turns counterclockwise and slows.

items.q: A grinding wheel speeds up from 20.0 rad/s to 50.0 rad/s with a constant angular acceleration of 6.00 rad/s². Through what angle does it turn while speeding up?

mistakes.why: Value: that ignores the starting angular velocity. Use ω² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ with ω₀ = 20.0 rad/s.
Value: that squares the change in ω. The equation uses ω² − ω₀², not (ω − ω₀)².

why.correct: No time is given, so use ω² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ: Δθ = (50.0² − 20.0²)/(2 × 6.00) = 2100/12.0 = 175 rad.

items.q: A rigid wheel turns about a fixed axle. Which statement is true for the points on the wheel?
options: Each point turns through the same angle in a given time
Points farther from the axle turn through larger angles
Each point moves the same distance in a given time
Points near the axle have a larger angular velocity

why.correct: A rigid system keeps its shape, so every point turns through the same angle in the same time: one θ, one ω and one α describe the whole wheel.
options: Right: that is what it means for the wheel to be a rigid system.
Points farther out travel farther, but they turn through the same angle.
Points farther from the axle trace bigger circles, so they move farther.
Every point of a rigid wheel shares one angular velocity.

items.q: A fan turns counterclockwise and speeds up with a constant angular acceleration. Predict how each quantity changes over the next second.

variables.name: Angular velocity
variables.why: α has the same sign as ω, so ω grows by α each second.

variables.name: Angular acceleration
variables.why: The angular acceleration is constant, as stated.

variables.name: Angle turned in each second
variables.why: The fan is turning faster, so it covers a larger angle each second.

why.correct: With constant α in the direction of ω, ω increases steadily; the faster it turns, the larger the angle covered each second, while α itself stays the same.

items.q: A wheel starts from rest and turns with constant positive angular acceleration. What does its graph of angle θ against time look like?
options: A curve that gets steeper with time
A straight line through the origin
A horizontal line
A curve that levels off

why.correct: The slope of a θ-t graph is ω. With constant positive α, ω grows steadily, so the graph is a parabola that gets steeper with time, just like x-t for constant a.
options: Right: θ = ½αt², and the slope of θ-t is ω, which keeps growing.
A straight θ-t line means constant ω, not constant α.
A flat θ-t line means the wheel is not turning.
Leveling off would mean ω is falling, so α would be negative.
